name: Interruption / Cancel
summary: Cancel side-effectful agent work with immediate acknowledgment, an honest account of what already happened, and no silent continuation after the user says stop.
problem: Agent work runs long and has side effects. A cancel affordance that is missing, slow to acknowledge, or dishonest about what already happened converts user control into theater: clicks appear ignored while the host aborts asynchronously, late tool results overwrite the cancelled state, and completed side effects vanish from view as if the work never ran.
useWhen: Multi-step agent work runs long enough that users need a way out mid-flight
The work has side effects the user may want to stop before they multiply
Cancellation maps to a real host mechanism (AbortController, job cancellation) that stops future work
dontUseWhen: The work is effectively instantaneous and a cancel control could never be reached in time
Only the rendering of a text stream needs stopping — streaming-response owns that case
Cancellation cannot actually stop anything; a fake cancel is worse than none

anatomy.description: Visible control, present while work runs, whose accessible name names the work being cancelled.
Immediate acknowledgment that cancellation was requested, distinct from the running indicator.

Settled account of the work: what completed before the stop, what was stopped, and whether the work finished before cancellation took effect. Focusable programmatically (tabindex="-1") as the recovery target when the cancel control is removed.
Progress display for the running work that the cancel control governs.

states.description: Work is executing; the cancel control is available.
The user asked to stop; the host has not yet settled. Acknowledged immediately and never silently exited.
The host stopped the work; the outcome summary reports completed and stopped items.
The work finished — possibly before a pending cancellation took effect, which is disclosed.

constraints.statement: Activating the cancel control MUST move the component to the cancel-requested state within the same interaction, before the host acknowledges the cancellation.
constraints.rationale: Host-side aborts are asynchronous; a button that visibly does nothing until the abort lands reads as broken and invites rage clicks.
constraints.verification: Unit test: activating cancel changes the state and the announcement synchronously while the host still reports running work.

constraints.statement: The component MUST NOT re-enter the running state after cancellation is requested; progress arriving while cancellation is pending renders without resetting the state.
constraints.rationale: Tool results land after the user says stop; letting them flip the UI back to running tells the user their cancellation was ignored.
constraints.verification: Unit test: progress updates during cancel-requested update the progress display while the state attribute stays cancel-requested.

constraints.statement: When cancellation settles, the component MUST report which work completed before the stop and which work was stopped; side effects that occurred are listed, not hidden.
constraints.rationale: Cancel stops future work — it does not unsend the three emails that already went out. Hiding completed side effects converts an interruption into a lie.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the cancelled state renders the completed-work and stopped-work lists supplied at settle.

constraints.statement: If the host reports completion while cancellation is pending, the component MUST settle to completed and disclose that the work finished before cancellation took effect.
constraints.rationale: Pretending a finished task was cancelled misstates what happened in the world; the user needs to know the side effects are the completed ones.
constraints.verification: Unit test: cancel, then settle with a completed outcome; the state is completed and the race disclosure is rendered.

constraints.statement: The cancel control MUST NOT require a confirmation step; cancelling stops future work rather than destroying existing work.
constraints.rationale: Confirmation friction belongs on destructive actions. Cancel is the safe action — every second spent in a dialog is another side effect landing.
constraints.verification: Unit test: a single activation of the cancel control invokes the cancel callback exactly once with no intermediate dialog.

constraints.statement: The cancel control MUST be keyboard-operable with an accessible name that names the work being cancelled.
constraints.rationale: A screen reader user hearing 'button, Cancel' in a page of controls cannot tell which running work it governs.
constraints.verification: Unit test plus axe: the control is a native button whose accessible name includes the work label.

constraints.statement: The cancel-requested acknowledgment and the settled outcome MUST be announced through a polite live region.
constraints.rationale: Without announcements, a screen reader user who activates cancel gets silence followed by a content change they have to discover.
constraints.verification: Unit test: the live region text changes at cancel-request and again at settle.

constraints.statement: If the cancel control holds focus when it is removed, focus MUST move to the work region rather than being dropped on the document body.
constraints.rationale: The cancel control disappears at the moment it is most likely to be focused — the user just pressed it. Browser default drops focus to the body, stranding keyboard users.
constraints.verification: Unit test: focus the cancel control, request cancellation, and assert focus is on the work region, not the body.

constraints.statement: Escape SHOULD request cancellation while focus is within the component.
constraints.rationale: Escape is the universal stop gesture; supporting it keeps this pattern consistent with streaming-response.
constraints.verification: Unit test: Escape keydown inside the component while running requests cancellation.

constraints.statement: Implementations MAY pair the cancelled outcome with an undo or rollback action for side effects that support it.
constraints.rationale: Where completed side effects are reversible, offering the reversal next to the honest summary is the natural next step.
constraints.verification: Code review: rollback, if present, is scoped to the listed completed work.

wcagCriteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
wcagCriteria.relevance: Long-running agent work is a process the user must be able to stop; the cancel control is the mechanism.

wcagCriteria.name: Status Messages
wcagCriteria.relevance: The acknowledgment and outcome are status changes that must reach assistive technology without focus moves.

wcagCriteria.name: Name, Role, Value
wcagCriteria.relevance: The cancel control's name must carry which work it stops.

keyboard.action: Reaches the cancel control in document order while work runs.
Requests cancellation while focus is within the component (SHOULD-level).

screenReader.behavior: Polite announcement that cancellation was requested and the work is stopping.
Polite announcement of the outcome: cancelled, completed, or completed before cancellation took effect.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus never moves while it is outside the component. The single exception: if the cancel control holds focus when it is removed, focus moves to the work region (tabindex="-1") instead of being dropped on the body.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Running and cancelling indicators do not animate under prefers-reduced-motion; state changes render instantly.

do: Name the work in the cancel control: 'Cancel: drafting 7 emails', not 'Cancel'.
Wire cancellation to a real abort mechanism (AbortController, job API) before rendering the control.
Keep the outcome summary in the same place the progress lived, so the eye does not have to hunt for what happened.
dont: Do not confirm cancellation with a dialog; cancel is the safe action.
Do not let late tool results re-open the running state after the user said stop.
Do not report 'Cancelled' when the work actually finished — disclose the race.

references.title: MDN: AbortController
references.note: The host-side mechanism this pattern's cancel control should be wired to.
